title: api-try-and-scale-voice-pricing-explainer
content:
Purpose:
A concise working brief to bake a developer-first landing/quickstart + pricing microcopy that scales from hobby projects to early production. Goal is to reduce friction for the first API call, make cost expectations crystal, and provide language the product pages, emails, and onboarding flows can reuse.

TL;DR:
- Core message: "Fast to try. Predictable to scale." Developers want an immediate win (call in <3 minutes) and predictable economics once usage grows.
- Two paths: Trial-first (free credits + sample prompts) and Commit-first (reserved pricing for early production).
- Pricing copy should separate unit economics (tokens/embedding units) from optional committed discounts, and emphasize observability (per-route cost breakdown).

Target personas:
- Indie/solo devs: care about free credits, examples, and a minimal friction SDK.
- Early-stage startups/PMs: want repeatable quickstarts and an expected cost per user metric.
- Platform/engineering leads: care about predictable throughput, reserved capacity, and SLA language.

Key developer-first value props (short lines for hero / bullets):
- "Make your first inference in minutes — SDKs and samples for JS, Python, and curl."
- "Metered pricing that scales: pay as you go or reserve capacity with predictable invoices."
- "Turnkey performance: latency profiles and cost estimates for each model so you pick what fits your SLOs."
- "Visibility into spend — token-level breakdowns by endpoint, model and user."

Supporting evidence / signals to include inline:
- "Benchmarked: p50 p99 latency for common prompt sizes" (link to public benchmarks).
- "Cost calculator: estimated cost per monthly active user for sample workloads."
- "Customer quote: 'We shipped a prototype in a day and cut per-token cost 3x with caching suggestions.'"

Quickstart angles (copy + flows):
1) "Hello API — 90 seconds" (dev-first hero CTA)
   - Microcopy: "No signup card needed — create an API key and run the sample in <2 minutes."
   - Steps shown: create key -> npm install @redwood/infer -> run sample -> view response streaming
   - Visual: inline code block with single curl and single JS example

2) "Prototype to Prod — 1 hour" (for PMs / small teams)
   - Microcopy: "Ship a prototype, measure latency and cost, then choose a production lane (payg | reserved)."
   - Steps: quickstart app template -> test harness with 10k synthetic requests -> cost estimator -> optional reserved capacity button

3) "Platform Onramp — SLA-ready" (for platform teams)
   - Microcopy: "Pin model versions, reserve capacity, and enable canary rollout policies with a single toggle."

Suggested UX/pricing microcopy (short lines to reuse across site and emails):
- Headline: "Try the API free. Scale with predictable pricing."
- Subhead: "Free credits for prototyping. Transparent per-token pricing with optional committed discounts."
- CTA variants: "Try in 2 minutes" / "Estimate cost for your app" / "Get reserved pricing"

Pricing language — explanation scaffolding (developer-friendly):
- "Meter: We charge per 1k input + output tokens for text generation and per 1k tokens for embeddings. Use our cost estimator to see how this maps to MAU for your app."
- "Free credits: New accounts receive X credits (example section showing how credits map to calls)."
- "Reserved capacity: Commit to a monthly GPU pool for lower per-token cost and burst protection. Reserve pricing is billed as a monthly commitment and reduces unit price by up to Y% depending on term."
- "Overage & bursts: If you exceed reserved capacity we'll automatically route low-priority requests to pay-as-you-go models (no silent failures). You can opt out if strict isolation is required."

Pricing examples (copy-ready):
- "Prototype: free credits + PAYG. Example: 100 calls/day at 256 tokens ≈ $Z/month."
- "Early production: reserve 1 GPU equivalent for $A/month — estimated $B per 1M tokens after discount."

Competitive callouts / positioning notes (what to say and avoid):
- Callouts to emphasize: latency predictability, token-level observability, reserved capacity guarantees, built-in fallback policies. These are Redwood strengths versus broad cloud endpoints.
- Avoid naming competitor prices directly on site; instead provide comparative scenes in sales decks and benchmarks: "Faster p99 for common prompts; lower effective cost when using prefix caching."
- One-line rebuttals to expected objections:
  - "Why not just use model-provider APIs?" -> "Our runtime and tooling reduce tail latency and unit cost so you get production predictability without building ops glue."
  - "Isn’t reserved capacity expensive?" -> "Reserved capacity buys predictable invoices and consistent latency — important at scale; PAYG remains available for bursty traffic."

Onboarding telemetry and metrics to present to users during trial:
- Live: p50/p95 latency, tokens consumed, cost estimate for the current session, suggested batching/quantization tips (derived from Optimize).
- Post-trial/email: projected monthly cost at current usage, recommended next steps (keep PAYG / reserve capacity / open contract).

Copy experiments (A/B ideas):
- A: "Try the API in 2 minutes" vs B: "Ship an LLM prototype in under an hour" — measure activation (first 5 calls) and time-to-first-paid-call.
- Experiment pricing microcopy: "Estimated cost per active user" vs "Estimated cost per 1M tokens" — measure clarity and conversion to reserved pricing signups.

FAQ snippets to include on quickstart page:
- "How much will this cost me?" -> short answer with link to estimator.
- "Can I switch from PAYG to Reserved?" -> "Yes, seamless upgrade; reserved becomes effective at next billing cycle; historical usage included in recommendations."
- "Do you support private deployments?" -> "Yes — our Private product offers the same API with control plane in your VPC. Contact sales for pricing."

Next steps / action items (owner tags):
- Draft landing hero microcopy and two CTA variants (owner: Ava Chen) — due 2025-11-08.
- Build 2-minute quickstart code snippet pack for JS/Python/cURL and host as gist (owner: Jonah Patel) — due 2025-11-12.
- Add cost-estimator widget copy and 3 example workloads (owner: Sofia Morales + eng) — due 2025-11-19.
- Sales enable: one-pager with comparison bullets to platform endpoints and managed runtimes (owner: Ethan Li) — due 2025-11-22.

Raw copy snippets you can copy-paste:
- "Try Redwood Inference free — get started in under 2 minutes with SDKs and sample prompts."
- "Pay as you go or reserve capacity for predictable pricing and enterprise SLAs."
- "Token-level cost visibility so you can optimize where it matters."

Notes / open questions (working):
- What exact free credit amount resonates? Bench tests suggest showing credits as "~X calls with a 256 token prompt" is more tangible.
- Do we surface competitor latency/price graphs publicly or keep them in gated benchmarks? Recommend gated for now.

Appendix: example 2-minute quickstart (text block for site)
- Step 0: Create account and copy API key
- Step 1: npm i @redwood/infer
- Step 2: run the example:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"Summarize the following: ...","max_tokens":128 }'
- Step 3: See streaming response; view token usage in Console -> Usage -> Live session

End of brief.

Internal status: rough draft — ready for product + eng review for accuracy on reserved pricing mechanics and benchmark links.
